title: Nana Patekar's Decade-Long Fight for India's Farmers Earns Unlikely Political Praise
excerpt: The veteran Bollywood actor, who founded NAAM Foundation in 2015 after witnessing farmer suicides in Maharashtra, has emerged as a rare non-partisan voice on agrarian distress — and recently partnered with the UP government on a viral cyber awareness campaign.
body:
• Nana Patekar's NAAM Foundation, co-founded with actor Makrand Anaspure in 2015, has provided financial aid to hundreds of farmer families across Maharashtra's drought-hit Marathwada and Vidarbha regions
  • CM Yogi Adityanath's UP government cast Patekar in a cyber fraud awareness short film that garnered over 17 lakh views, marking an unusual collaboration between the actor-activist and the BJP administration
  • NAAM Foundation raised Rs 60 crore in its first six months through public donations and has expanded into water conservation, disaster relief, and support for army martyrs' families
  • India continues to record thousands of farmer suicides annually, with Maharashtra alone accounting for roughly a quarter of the national total

Nana Patekar has spent a decade walking the fields of drought-ravaged Maharashtra, handing checks to widows, digging wells, and telling politicians to stop exploiting farmers. Now the veteran actor's work has drawn an unexpected endorsement — the Uttar Pradesh government, under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, tapped Patekar for a high-profile cyber crime awareness campaign, recognizing his credibility as a public figure who acts rather than postures.

From Bollywood to the Fields

Patekar's involvement with farmer welfare began in 2015, when a wave of suicides swept through Maharashtra's Marathwada and Vidarbha regions. The National Award-winning actor, known for intense roles in films like Ab Tak Chhappan and Natsamrat, visited Beed district and met over 200 widows of farmers who had taken their lives.

https://x.com/shrikantyerule/status/2088302362528199162

"I had kept some money, about Rs 1.5 crore, aside to buy a car," Patekar later recalled. "When I saw the wife, children and parents of a farmer who had committed suicide, I decided I would donate that money."

Together with fellow Marathi actor Makrand Anaspure, Patekar founded the NAAM Foundation. The organization raised Rs 80 lakh on the day it opened its bank account, and Rs 60 crore within six months. Actor Akshay Kumar contributed Rs 90 lakh, and cricketer Ajinkya Rahane donated Rs 5 lakh.

The Work on the Ground

NAAM Foundation's efforts have extended beyond direct financial aid. The organization has funded water conservation projects, excavation work for irrigation, and provided support to families of army martyrs. Patekar and Anaspure personally visited families of 113 farmers in Latur and Osmanabad districts, distributing Rs 15,000 each.

"If someone knocks at your car window, don't treat them like beggars. They are farmers. They are helpless. They need food, water and access to toilets."

— Nana Patekar

Patekar has remained pointedly non-partisan in his advocacy, criticizing successive governments — Congress and BJP alike — for failing farmers. "It's not a matter of one or two years. We've been failing our farmers since the last sixty-eight years," he told NDTV. He has also argued that loan waivers alone are insufficient, calling for fair crop pricing and emotional support alongside financial relief.

The UP Government Connection

The Uttar Pradesh Police, acting on directives from CM Adityanath to strengthen cybercrime prevention, released a short film starring Patekar that warned citizens about "digital arrest" scams. The film, directed by Raj Shandilya of Dream Girl fame, was inspired by a real incident in Kanpur. It garnered over 10.42 lakh views on YouTube, 1.26 lakh on X, and reached 5 lakh people through WhatsApp channels within four days.

The collaboration was notable: Patekar lending his credibility to a BJP state government's public service campaign, despite his history of calling out political failures on farmer issues.

The Bigger Picture

India recorded over 10,000 farmer suicides in 2021, the most recent year with complete NCRB data. Maharashtra alone accounted for roughly a quarter of the total. Despite government schemes and periodic loan waivers, the structural issues driving agrarian distress — water scarcity, inadequate crop pricing, fragmented landholdings, and limited access to institutional credit — remain largely unresolved.

Patekar's decade-long engagement stands out because it has persisted long after the news cameras moved on. NAAM Foundation continues to operate, and Patekar continues to visit villages. "Paisa is a by-product," he once said. "I feel secure by doing this. Those people will remember me for life."

nri_angle: Patekar's farmer advocacy resonates with the Indian diaspora concerned about agrarian distress back home, while his cyber awareness campaign highlights scam risks that also affect NRIs.
